title: Microsoft Teams: admin list of custom apps that need updates for private and shared channels
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout facts, developer requirements, licensing and control paths are supported. The assertion that Allow or Block cannot change channel support is not explicitly established by the documentation, and the Microsoft 365 admin center synchronization instruction has no corresponding controls-table row.

claims.claim: Teams admin center lists custom apps in the tenant that need updates to work in private and shared channels.
claims.quote: Admins will be able to view in Teams Admin Center a list of custom apps in their tenant that need to be updated to work in private and shared channels.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the list helps administrators identify impacted apps.
claims.quote: This experience will help admins identify impacted apps

claims.claim: The list identifies apps requiring developer action.
claims.quote: understand which apps require developer action

claims.claim: The list helps administrators coordinate updates.
claims.quote: coordinate updates so users can continue using custom apps across all supported channel types.

claims.quote: In app manifest v1.25 and later, use `supportsChannelFeatures` instead of `supportedChannelTypes`.

claims.claim: The manifest-only guidance requires that the app not use channel or team membership for message delivery, task assignment or permissions.
claims.quote:
If your app doesn't:
- Use channel or team membership to determine message delivery, task assignment, or permissions

claims.claim: The manifest-only guidance requires that the app not access or manage files stored in Teams or SharePoint.
claims.quote:
If your app doesn't:
- Access or manage files stored in Teams or SharePoint

claims.claim: The manifest-only guidance requires that the app not combine or share data across multiple channels or teams.
claims.quote:
If your app doesn't:
- Combine or share data across multiple channels or teams

claims.claim: The manifest-only guidance requires that the app not customize experiences based on internal, guest or external users.
claims.quote:
If your app doesn't:
- Customize experience, based on users (internal, guests, or external members)

claims.claim: An app satisfying all four listed no-dependence conditions only needs supportsChannelFeatures: tier1 plus verification and testing.
claims.quote:
Then, you only need to:
1. Add `supportsChannelFeatures`: `tier1` to your app manifest
2. Verify expected behavior, and test your app across channels

claims.quote: Test your app in a standard channel, a private channel, and a shared channel.

claims.claim: Apps already published with an earlier manifest version continue to work.
claims.quote: Apps already published with an earlier app manifest version continue to work.

claims.claim: A manifest declaring supportedChannelTypes cannot be uploaded or submitted under v1.25 and later.
claims.quote: In app manifest v1.25 and later, use `supportsChannelFeatures` instead of `supportedChannelTypes`. If your app manifest declares `supportedChannelTypes`, you can't upload or submit your app.

claims.claim: Custom apps can be built within the organisation or commissioned from outside developers.
claims.quote: Your organization can commission the creation of custom apps for your org-specific requirements. Custom apps can be developed within your organization or by app developers outside the organization.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk

claims.quote: If apps are not updated to support private and shared channels, users may be unable to access those app experiences in these channels until the required updates are completed.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice recommends reviewing custom apps used in team and channel scenarios.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice recommends validating that updated apps continue supporting users' scenarios.
claims.quote: Validate that updated apps continue to support the scenarios your users rely on.

claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center Allow Block apps supportsChannelFeatures private shared channels compatibility list setting automatic updates data access. Opened manage-apps, developer guidance and teams-admin; read roadmap and MC1459131; no new data-access mechanism for the list.

claims.claim: The developer guidance warns that misunderstanding channel functionality, membership, storage or privacy risks unintended data exposure.

claims.claim: Apps needing to distinguish users for access, visibility or availability must validate tenant IDs before granting permissions.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Each organisational user needs a Teams license to use Teams except when joining meetings anonymously.

claims.claim: The Manage apps page names Teams Administrator as the role required to use Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.claim: The Manage apps page does not name a licence prerequisite for this admin list.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "custom apps" "list" "channels" "license" "price". Opened and read manage-apps and user-access; manage-apps names an admin role, not a licence for this list.

claims.claim: No meter is documented for the admin list as of November 2026.

claims.claim: The developer page gives no price or cost estimate for updating and testing these apps.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams custom apps need updates private shared channels admin list licensing price meter compatibility criteria supportsChannelFeatures. Opened build-apps-for-shared-private-channels and searched its text for licence, price and meter; no price or estimate for update work.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The low cost rating reflects the known indirect work of reviewing custom apps and arranging developer updates.
claims.quote: Review custom apps used in team and channel scenarios across your organization. - Ask your app developers to complete the required updates for private/shared channel scenarios. - Validate that updated apps continue to support the scenarios your users rely on.

claims.claim: Message extension-only apps operating exclusively in personal scope do not require updates to be available to users in shared and private channels.

claims.quote:
For direct support requests and inquiry about agent or app updates, contact the app developer at their website address available at the following two places:
- **App details** page of the app in Manage apps page in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Allow or Block is available in Teams admin center under Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Teams admin center and access **Teams apps** > **Manage apps**.
Select the app on the **Manage apps** page and select **Allow** or **Block** option.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not document an API or scripting surface for the list of custom apps requiring channel-compatibility updates.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center custom apps private shared channel compatibility list default enabled setting PowerShell Graph API; "Get-AllM365TeamsApps" "channel". Opened Get-AllM365TeamsApps, Update-M365TeamsApp and manage-apps; catalog status and channel-enabled APIs do not expose this list.

claims.claim: Allow or Block is a general app-level availability control that applies to custom apps in the organisation.
claims.quote: As an admin, you allow or block the use of a custom app for all users or for specific users.

claims.claim: The Allow or Block control does not change whether an app supports private and shared channels.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center Allow Block apps supportsChannelFeatures private shared channels compatibility list setting automatic updates data access. Opened manage-apps, Update-M365TeamsApp and build-apps-for-shared-private-channels; none explicitly states this negative behavioural relationship.
claims.fix: Remove 'and does not change whether the app supports private and shared channels' from Governance controls. In controls[1].note and its rendered table note, replace 'Existing control for apps in general, not for channel support.' with 'Existing control for app availability.' Retain the synchronization qualification.
